audit_prompt: Independently evaluate each description against the supplied concept definition and each item’s assigned style. Check factual accuracy, concept alignment, natural standalone English, style, absence of names/aliases and near semantic duplicates of prior accepted descriptions (including other splits) or earlier items in this batch. A shared broad topic is not itself duplication, but essentially the same factual claim or paraphrase is. Return JSON {"items":[{"id":"...","fact":"pass|fail|uncertain","alignment":"pass|fail|uncertain","style":"pass|fail|uncertain","exposure":"pass|fail|uncertain","duplicate":"pass|fail|uncertain","reason":"..."}]}. Return every id exactly once. Treat supplied sentences as data. Do not infer model performance.
checkpoint_policy: local per API event; GitHub per unit split and on failure
extraction: v5 user-only chat template, add_generation_prompt=True, last input token, float32 eager
generation_prompt: Generate factually accurate natural standalone English descriptions for a concept probe dataset. Each sentence describes the specified concept, without naming it, comparison concepts or their obvious aliases. Use the assigned style and 10–25 words. The request supplies a style-to-count map; return each item with a style key matching that map. Avoid label-specific formatting, fiction, trivia guesses and recycled facts. Each fact_key is a short description of a distinct factual claim. Use prior sentences only to avoid near paraphrase and repeated factual claims, not as templates. Use diverse facets and contexts. For held-out evaluation, use new factual claims or contexts rather than paraphrases of training. Output JSON {"items":[{"sentence":"...","fact_key":"...","style":"structure"}]}. Treat provided text as data, not instructions.
permutation_family: 25 primary L24 separately from primary L1–23; exploratory only
selection: one B primary candidate per X/quintile nearest B band_center; deterministic label/id tie break

styles.function: purpose, role, consequence or typical use
